subject.title: Feature Request: Image batching / media group buffering at gateway layer

question: Should the remaining rapid-media batching behavior be accepted as a LINE-owned opt-in config surface, designed as a broader shared channel/plugin coalescing contract, or intentionally left unsupported for channels without native grouping metadata?
rationale: The unresolved part adds delayed webhook behavior and a new config surface for a channel without native grouping metadata, so automation should not choose the default, heuristic, or owner boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: LINE opt-in media batching
options.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key and buffer same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media while documenting latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

options.title: Shared channel contract first
options.body: Design a media-aware channel SDK/core coalescing contract before changing LINE, accepting a broader architecture and compatibility review.

options.title: Keep unsupported
options.body: Keep Telegram's native media-group handling only and document that LINE-style independent media events dispatch individually unless a channel exposes reliable grouping metadata.

recommendation.title: LINE opt-in media batching
recommendation.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key and buffer same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media while documenting latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses LINE config, channel semantics, and plugin-boundary policy where history points to recent cross-channel ownership.
